findings.criterion: An effect the reviewer's compiled envelope denies (remote.*, git.mutate*; packages/skeleton/src/loadouts/entropy-reducer.ts:38-44) either cannot happen from the frozen copy or is visible in the receipt. docs/instance/entropy-reducer/README.md:130-131 says Claude shell confinement 'is instructed and then checked'.
findings.observed: freezeSubject (scripts/lib/entropy-review.mjs:334-345) makes the copy with `git clone --no-hardlinks --no-checkout <root>` and leaves `origin` in place. In this episode the copy's origin, for both fetch and push, is the operator's own checkout (<home>/Projects/DotLn). The review (:1111) and the refutation (:1490) both use freezeSubject. The claude-cli-print launch (packages/skeleton/src/worker-transport.ts:817-847) passes --safe-mode, so the project's hooks and deny list do not load, and it pre-approves Bash. The receipt watches the source through two things only: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` and the untracked listing (entropy-review.mjs:125-126, 210-231). Nothing records the source's refs or remotes. I built a clone the same way in the episode temp directory. From it, `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/escaped` created a branch in the source, and `--force` rewrote an existing branch that was not checked out (a66981ac -> e4c46109). Both pushes exited 0, and both witness digests stayed byte-identical (e3b0c442..., empty) before and after. I made no push to the operator's repository.
findings.expected: The frozen copy has no route back to its source: origin is removed, or its push URL refuses, right after the clone. Alternatively, or as well, the confinement record digests the source's refs (`git for-each-ref`) on both sides of the episode and flags or refuses a change, so the README's 'checked' claim covers ref writes. The README credits the Codex route's workspace-write sandbox, rooted at the copy, with confining its writes; I did not exercise that here.

standardization.rationale: Every review, every refutation, and any later route that freezes a subject inherits this channel. A precondition in freezeSubject that refuses to hand off a copy with a configured remote, plus a refs digest in the confinement record, runs on every dispatch. findings.observed: At e4c46109, `node scripts/docs-check.mjs` exits 0 and reports 28 current operator-word advisories against 332 historical. WO-188-D015 recorded 0 current on 2026-10-08. To see what each row matched, I instrumented docs-check in a scratch copy. About 5 of the 28 are verbatim operator replies with no capture digest, all in records dated after D015: WO-200-D002 (2026-10-12), WO-210-D024/evidence-1 (2026-10-14), WO-221-D028 and its evidence-1 (2026-10-19), and docs/verifications/WO-203/VER-001.md:149. The other ~22 are quote characters near the word 'operator' that are not operator speech: JSON finding arrays in final reviews, program output, or a quoted document phrase. So the condition has occurred and the check admits it. No planning document cites WO-188-D015 (0 files), and no register row tracks its reopening; FUP-71fc2efc208f597a was settled onto it but reopens only on a typed quotation. The 2026-10-19 pass's validation (docs/planning/standard-pass-2026-10-19.md:490) calls the advisories 'historical'. Run at that pass's own commit (899eeec1), the same function reports 24 current and 332 historical. A mutation drill on a synthetic root showed the advisory cannot separate these cases: a JSON finding array, a quoted product phrase and a quoted reply each yield one indistinguishable row, and a paraphrase yields none.
findings.expected: A planning pass re-disposes WO-188-D015, naming the qualifying records. The advisory, which stays advisory as D015 decided, separates attributed speech from incidental quote characters (inside JSON or code, or a quoted document term), so the reopening condition can be read without classifying every row by hand.

On the Claude route (--safe-mode, Bash pre-approved), a push from the copy writes refs into the source while both receipt witnesses stay byte-identical. Reproduced on throwaway repositories in TMPDIR only. Checked, not filed: kernel wildcard and resource semantics, skill-root parity, cited commands, index freshness, publish refusals, the WO-105 lane failure (known, allocated to WO-220), executor cold-start headroom of 33 bytes (operator-reserved). Notes: one deliberately denied Read tested --restricted; one incidental ls of a scratch extraction listed two tracked docs/intake directory names, no contents read. Scratch trees removed; subject unchanged. Awaiting operator disposition.
